_comment: #467: does the Authelia SSO stack need an LDAP server? Decision 2026-09-24: NO. Recorded
here with the condition that would change it.
Authelia uses authentication_backend: file with ONE user (infra-sec_authelia
src/templates/init.sh.tpl). Caddy protects routes with forward_auth plus the bearer
introspect path, and Authelia is also the OIDC provider. No live service is set up to
authenticate against LDAP: a scan for LDAP_ env vars and ldap:// or ldaps:// URLs outside
z_archive finds nothing. A directory with no consumers would be one more
container on the SSO critical path and would protect nothing.
Adding it would also cause an outage. Moving Authelia to an ldap backend restarts Authelia.
While it is down, every forward_auth route returns errors, and the bearer path does too,
because it goes through infra-sec_introspect-proxy into Authelia (a GLOBAL bearer outage).
Shipping infra-sec_caddy-public to change the routes also takes SSO down (#55). Neither
change is justified with zero consumers.
Checked by 9_others/test/test_sso_ldap_consumers.sh. It FAILS when an LDAP consumer
appears, so #467 gets looked at again, instead of that service quietly sending logins to
a directory that does not exist.
sso_gaps_2026_09_24: RESOLVED 2026-09-25 (#467 follow-up). Mail password stores: Stalwart is authoritative (imap. and smtps. on :443 already terminate there). Its activate hook has created every declared user from the same build.json users and pass_env as maddy since 2026-09-05, so the declarations no longer disagree; the 'maddy five, Stalwart two' count was measured 2026-09-04, before that hook. Radicale (calendar and contacts) now checks IMAP logins against Stalwart's IMAPS listener (declared imap_ssl port) instead of maddy. No password value was changed. Maddy's authdb is still declared for :25 inbound and rollback; retiring it is a separate change.

OPEN, by design. No live app uses Authelia's OIDC provider for its own sign-in. Gitea, Mattermost, PhotoPrism, HedgeDoc, Filebrowser, Umami and OpenObserve sit behind forward_auth and keep their own accounts as well. Each could use OIDC with the provider that already exists, which needs no new container.

RESOLVED 2026-09-25 where a route can take forward_auth, KEPT where it cannot. vault.: Vaultwarden's open signup is now off (SIGNUPS_ALLOWED=false; invitations still work). The route stays outside forward_auth because the Bitwarden apps and extension cannot answer an Authelia redirect, and it is WG-only. matrix. (continuwuity, public, registration by token) stays public: federation and Matrix clients cannot do forward_auth. chat. /api/v4/* stays a bypass: the Mattermost apps and bots need it and Mattermost authenticates them itself. IMAPS and SMTPS through SNI on :443, and Gitea SSH :2222, are not HTTP, so forward_auth cannot apply; each checks its own credentials.

RESOLVED 2026-09-25. The stale 'nocodb' OIDC client is deleted from infra-sec_authelia/src/oidc-clients.json. Deploying it restarts Authelia: forward_auth and the bearer path (via infra-sec_introspect-proxy) error for the length of the restart. The now-unused AUTHELIA_OIDC_CLIENT_NOCODB_SECRET is still in the sops files, because a value cannot be removed without the age key; drop it at the next secrets edit.
